skeleton:
Fried Eggs with Black Pudding Crumb

British · Easy · Serves 2

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The black pudding demoted to its best supporting role: crumbled into a hot pan and fried to dark, crunchy rubble, then scattered over crispy-edged fried eggs like the world's most British bacon crumb. It is the 5-minute upgrade that turns two plain fried eggs into a plate with texture, smoke, and iron-rich depth — and it uses the piece of black pudding that's too small to slice, which is the café economy in a single move.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The crumb

  • most renders its own)

The eggs

To serve

- **Crumble by hand, not knife** — torn pieces of uneven size fry into a mix of crunch and chew, which is the texture you want. Knife-diced goes uniform and bead-like. - **Skin off completely** — the skin fries to leather and ruins the crumb's bite. - One pan, two stages: crumb first (it renders the fat the eggs will fry in), eggs second.

Fried Eggs with Black Pudding Crumb

Prep: 5 minutes · Cook: 8 minutes · Total: 13 minutes · Serves 2

Ingredients

The crumb

  • 120 g black pudding, skin removed, crumbled into rough 1 cm pieces
  • 5 g butter (only if the pudding is lean — most renders its own)

The eggs

  • 4 large eggs (220 g)
  • 15 ml / 14 g neutral oil, or the crumb pan's rendered pudding fat
  • 1 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g black pepper

To serve

  • 2 slices (140 g) thick toast or fried bread
  • 5 g chives, snipped (optional)
  • Brown breakfast sauce

Instructions

  1. **Fry the crumb to dark rubble, 4–5 minutes.** Heat the pan (dry, or with the butter if the pudding is lean) over medium-high and add the crumbled pudding. Fry 4–5 minutes, stirring only every minute, until the pieces are dark and crisp at their edges — some almost black at the tips — and the pan holds a slick of rendered, mahogany fat. Checkpoint — the crumb rattles dryly when stirred, smells smoky and spiced, and no piece remains soft or greasy. It should crackle between finger and thumb.
  2. **Lift the crumb, fry the eggs in its fat, 3 minutes.** Scoop the crumb onto a plate, leaving the rendered fat in the pan — top up with a teaspoon of oil only if the pan looks dry. Over medium-high heat, crack in the eggs and fry to the crispy-edged master's spec: 90 seconds to 2 minutes, until the whites' edges go lace-gold and the yolks still run. Checkpoint — lace-edged whites, liquid yolks — cooked in the pudding's own spiced fat, which seasons the eggs before the salt touches them.
  3. **Build and eat immediately.** Eggs onto the toast, the dark crumb scattered generously over the whites — pressing it in lightly so it clings to the setting white — pepper over, chives if using. Checkpoint — the first bite: shatter of egg-lace, then the crumb's smoky crunch, then the yolk running through both. Three textures, one forkful, thirteen minutes' work.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Crumb chewy, not crunchyUnder-fried or crowdedMedium-high, one layer, the full 4–5 minutes to the rattle
Crumb burnt bitterHeat too high past minute 3, or stirred to constantlyDark is the aim, black is not; pull at the mahogany stage
Eggs greasyPan overloaded with rendered fatPour off to a 2–3 mm slick before the eggs
Crumb slid off the eggEgg fully set before the crumb landedScatter while the white's top face is still tacky from the pan

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **The crumb itself keeps** — fried crumb holds 3 days refrigerated in a sealed jar and re-crisps in 1 minute in a dry pan. It is the meal-prep move: crumb a whole pudding on Sunday, upgrade breakfasts all week. The eggs never hold. - **Variation — over bubble and squeak:** the crumb scattered over a fried bubble cake with a poached egg — the leftover plate's deluxe upgrade. - **Variation — over creamy scrambled eggs:** folded through at the off-heat finish, the crunch against the custard curds. - **The economy note:** this is what the last 120 g of every black pudding is for — the slices get the plated mornings; the crumb gets everything else.
